facts.statement: Alnashetri is an extinct alvarezsauroid theropod dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous of La Buitrera, Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Alnashetri is an extinct genus of alvarezsauroid coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) of La Buitrera, Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Alnashetri contains only one known species, Alnashetri cerropoliciensis.
facts.quote: It contains one known species, Alnashetri cerropoliciensis.

facts.statement: Alnashetri is known from two specimens, including a holotype with articulated hind limbs.
facts.quote: Alnashetri is known from two specimens, the holotype MPCA-477, contains the articulated hind limbs of a single individual.

facts.statement: A more complete skeleton of Alnashetri was discovered in 2014 and described in 2026.
facts.quote: A more complete skeleton was discovered in 2014 and described in 2026.

facts.statement: Alnashetri fossils were recovered from red sandstones in the upper part of the Candeleros Formation near the border with the Huincul Formation.
facts.quote: The specimens were recovered from massive red sandstones that form the upper part of the Candeleros Formation of the Rio Limay Subgroup, close to its border with the Huincul Formation.

facts.statement: While originally thought to be Late Cretaceous, the age of Alnashetri was re-dated to the early Albian, approximately 111.4 to 106.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Originally suggested to be the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, the maximum depositional age of both the Candeleros Formation and the overlying Huincul Formation is re-dated to the early Albian by Maniel et al. (2026), approximately 111.4 ± 1.1 Ma and 106.2 ± 1.0 Ma respectively.

facts.statement: Alnashetri was first described and named by Peter J. Makovicky, Sebastián Apesteguía, and Federico A. Gianechini in 2012.
facts.quote: Alnashetri was first described and named by Peter J. Makovicky, Sebastián Apesteguía, and Federico A. Gianechini in 2012

facts.statement: The name Alnashetri comes from the Tehuelche language and means "slender thighs," referring to the animal's long, thin hind legs.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Günün-a-kunna dialect of the Tehuelche language, meaning "slender thighs" in reference to long and slender hind limbs of the holotype.

facts.statement: The species name cerropoliciensis honors the village of Cerro Policía for helping with fieldwork since the site was discovered in 1999.
facts.quote: The specific name cerropoliciensis honors the nearby small village of Cerro Policía for the generous assistance from its residents in fieldwork efforts at La Buitrera locality since its discovery in 1999.

facts.statement: Alnashetri is a small, non-avian coelurosaur dinosaur.
facts.quote: Alnashetri is a small non-avian coelurosaur.

facts.statement: Alnashetri was only 60 cm long and 35 cm high, making it the smallest alvarezsauroid found to date.
facts.quote: Medía apenas 60 cm de largo y 35 de alto, por lo que es el alvarezsauroide más pequeño hallado hasta el momento.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis initially placed Alnashetri within the group Alvarezsauroidea.
facts.quote: Therefore, its phylogenetic position was initially tested in a cladistic matrix used to widely explore coelurosaurian interrelationships. This preliminary analysis found Alnashetri to nest within Alvarezsauroidea.

facts.statement: Later studies recovered Alnashetri as a basal alvarezsauroid, more derived than Xiyunykus and Bannykus but outside the family Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: Meso et al. (2024) recovered Alnashetri in a more basal position within Alvarezsauroidea, more derived than Xiyunykus and Bannykus of Early Cretaceous China, but outside of the more exclusive family Alvarezsauridae.

facts.statement: Alnashetri belongs to the superfamily Alvarezsauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Alvarezsauroidea

facts.statement: Alnashetri lived in South America during the early Late Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago between the Cenomanian and Turonian stages.
facts.quote: un dinosaurio terópodo alvarezsauroide que vivió a principios del período Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente 95 millones de años entre el Cenomaniense y el Turoniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a partial left femur, distal parts of both tibiae, a right fibula, proximal tarsals, a nearly complete right metatarsus, and parts of the left foot bones.
facts.quote: El holotipo consiste en un fémur izquierdo parcial, partes distales de ambas tibias, una fíbula derecha, tarsos proximales de ambos tobillos, un metatarso derecho casi completo, partes proximal y distal de los metapodiales derechos y el dígito pedal III izquierdo.

facts.statement: A more complete specimen, MPCA Pv377, was inferred to be a female.
facts.quote: El ejemplar MPCA Pv377, un individuo mucho más completo del cual se infiere que pudo haber sido una hembra.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the evidence supporting Alnashetri's placement in Alvarezsauroidea is reliable, as it relies heavily on ankle anatomy which may produce false results.
facts.quote: The evidence supporting this relationship originates in the detailed anatomy of the ankle, however, and this concentration of character support within a single anatomical region may create false results.

facts.statement: Alnashetri is classified as a basal alvarezsaurid within the Alvarezsauroidea group.
facts.quote: Este análisis preliminar encontró que Alnashetri se alojaba dentro de los Alvarezsauroidea.

facts.statement: Alnashetri is considered a basal alvarezsaurid in a polytomy with other alvarezsaurids from the Neuquén Basin.
facts.quote: Alnashetri fue considerado como un alvarezsáurido basal, en una politomía con otros alvarezsáuridos de la cuenca Neuquén.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Alnashetri is Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Alvarezsauridae

facts.statement: Alnashetri is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Alnashetri lived during the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: A new specimen of Alnashetri cerropoliciensis was discovered in the Candeleros Formation in Argentina and reported by Makovicky et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: Makovicky et al. (2026) report the discovery of a new specimen of Alnashetri cerropoliciensis from the Candeleros Formation (Argentina)

facts.statement: Researchers interpret a Late Jurassic theropod vertebra, a theropod astragalus from Wyoming formerly referred to Coelurus fragilis, and Calamosaurus foxi as alvarezsauroids.
facts.quote: the authors also interpret the Late Jurassic theropod vertebra described by Makovicky (1997), the theropod astragalus YPM 9163 from Como Bluff (Morrison Formation, Wyoming, United States; formerly referred to Coelurus fragilis) and Calamosaurus foxi as alvarezsauroids

facts.statement: The evolutionary history of alvarezsauroids is interpreted as having a Pangaean ancestral distribution.
facts.quote: interpreting it as having Pangaean ancestral distribution.

facts.statement: Due to the fragmentary nature of the holotype skeleton, Alnashetri lacks synapomorphies that would allow for a precise assignment to a particular ceratosaurian clade.
facts.quote: debido a la naturaleza fragmentaria del esqueleto del holotipo este carece de sinapomorfias que pudieran permitir una asignación certera a un clado de celurosaurios en particular.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the concentration of supporting traits within a single anatomical region, such as the ankle, can create false phylogenetic results.
facts.quote: no obstante que la concentración de rasgos que apoyen la idea dentro de una sola región anatómica puede crear resultados falsos.

rejected.quote: It can be differentiated from all other coelurosaurs in the possession of a low ridge on the distal end of the tibia, which separates the rostral surface for articulation with the astragalus from the outer face of the lateral malleolus and which extends up the shaft of the tibia dorsal to the tip of the ascending process of the astragalus.
